mathgap.title: Directed More-Than Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Translate comparative statements of the form 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B' into the equation A = B + N (or A = B - N), preserving the sign.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement explicitly says 'A has N more (or fewer) items than B'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'A has 5 more items than B' as A = B - 5, reversing the sign.

mathgap.title: Immediate Direct Assignment Update
mathgap.principle: A direct count statement (e.g., 'A has N items') sets the current value of A to N at that point in the narrative, and later statements may modify it.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a sentence that gives an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Treating a later transfer as not changing a previously assigned count, leaving the count fixed.

mathgap.title: Temporal Consistency of Transfers and Relational Statements
mathgap.principle: Process statements sequentially; when a transfer 'X gives N to Y' appears, immediately subtract N from X and add N to Y, and use these updated counts for any later statements involving X or Y.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a transfer statement is encountered.
mathgap.example: Processing 'X gives 3 to Y' by only subtracting 3 from X and ignoring the addition to Y, causing later equations to use the wrong value for Y.

mathgap.title: Full Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: For sentences equating two differences, translate them into the form (A - B) = (C - D), preserving the order of names on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says 'the number of X has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of A and B'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'the number of X has more than Y equals the difference between A and B' as X = Y + (A - B) instead of (X - Y) = (A - B).

mathgap.title: Quantity Modification (Multiplication and Subtraction)
mathgap.principle: When a statement modifies a count by multiplication, division, or subtraction (e.g., 'X increases by N times' or 'X decreases by N'), apply the appropriate arithmetic operation to X's current count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence describes a multiplicative or subtractive change to a count.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'X increases by 2 times' as X = X + 2 instead of X = X * 2.

mathgap.title: Redistribute Equally Among Group
mathgap.principle: If a group of people redistributes their items so that each ends up with the same amount, compute the total sum of their items and divide by the group size.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement says a set of people share or redistribute items equally.
mathgap.example: Failing to divide the total equally, leaving each person with the original amount.

mathgap.title: Comprehensive Constraint Extraction
mathgap.principle: Gather every constraint implied by each statement, even those that do not directly involve the queried person, to ensure enough equations for solving the system.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Throughout the problem, as each statement is read.
mathgap.example: Ignoring a relational statement that does not mention the target person, leading to an underdetermined system.

mathgap.title: Signed More-Than Difference Equality Interpretation
mathgap.principle: Within a difference equality, treat a phrase like 'the number of X has more than Y' as the signed difference X - Y, not the absolute value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a difference equality includes a 'has more than' phrase.
mathgap.example: Treating 'X has more than Y' as |X - Y|, losing sign information.

mathgap.title: Signed Difference Phrase Interpretation
mathgap.principle: When a phrase contains 'the difference between the number of X and Y', interpret it as the signed subtraction X - Y, preserving the order as stated.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a statement mentions 'difference between the number of X and Y'.
mathgap.example: Interpreting 'difference between X and Y' as |X - Y|, discarding sign.

mathgap.description: Treating ‘difference between the number of X and Y’ as absolute value instead of signed subtraction.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase sounds like a magnitude, leading the model to drop the sign.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the two names and interpret the phrase as X - Y.

mathgap.description: Delaying the effect of transfer statements until after all other statements.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model treats transfers as a separate phase rather than as immediate updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer instantly, updating both giver and receiver before processing later statements.

mathgap.description: Considering a direct count as a fixed initial value that cannot be changed by later transfers.
mathgap.why_it_happens: Misunderstanding that direct assignments set the current value, not an immutable baseline.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Treat direct counts as the current value at that point; later transfers can modify it.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting a difference equality as a direct assignment to a single variable, ignoring the second term (including assuming positivity).
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model simplifies the equality to a single side, losing the relational nature.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Translate difference equalities to (A - B) = (C - D) without dropping any term.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increases by N times' as addition or division instead of multiplication.
mathgap.why_it_happens: The phrase 'times' is ambiguous; the model may treat it as additive.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Recognize 'increases by N times' means multiply the current count by N.
